strategyPosture: Treat index-level calm as leadership rotation, not broad health: stay research-first on the DATA_AHEAD dislocations (AVGO, BWXT, VST, APP, NOW, NXT, MDB, CLS) with sizing only after thesis verification per the screened posture, and keep credit — HY OAS at 3.02, SLOOS at 0% — as the tripwire that would convert rotation into rollover.

themes.counterRead: The rotation read is historically consistent — weak mega-cap momentum plus loose credit is not a broad rollover. But the divergence is real and concentrated in the index's heaviest weights: if credit flips (HY OAS toward 4.0, SLOOS rising), the rotation thesis breaks and this becomes a rollover. Holding-level impact is already visible: NFLX, a Core holding, is a 1-month laggard at -13.84%.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average -11.33% from their 52-week highs, a 9.23-point divergence gap versus SPY. TSLA is the weakest at -28.9% off its high; only NVDA is near its peak (-3.4%). Small caps confirm the narrowness: IWM is -5.13% over the past month and -6.73% over three months. Credit, however, shows no stress: HY OAS is 3.02 and bank lending standards (SLOOS) read 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover: index calm masks Mag7 weakness
themes.narrative: The S&P 500 sits just 2.1% off its 52-week high and flat over the past month (-0.24%), implying broad market health going into Q4.
themes.watchFor: HY OAS breaking above 4.0 or SLOOS rising off 0% — either invalidates the rotation read; IWM closing its 3-month -6.73% gap would confirm breadth is finally participating.

themes.counterRead: VST's revenue inflection still reads DETERIORATING (vs RECOVERY for BWXT, NXT, and the software names), so the trough is not confirmed across the complex — the setup is fundamentals-ahead-of-price, but VST needs the inflection flip before sizing. The equipment-names rebound (GEV, ETN, PWR +7.21% 1m) suggests the market is re-pricing the supply chain before the IPPs.
themes.dataAnchor: The independent power producers are far deeper in drawdown than the narrative justifies: VST is -36.3% off its 52-week high while growing revenue +19.1% YoY with a 2.6x P/S and $1.17M of insider buying at the trough; NXT is -52.2% off its high with revenue +20.3% YoY; BWXT is -43.3% off its high (RSI 32.5, score 77 tier B) as a Level-2 supplier to the still-active nuclear theme. Meanwhile the Dimon headline puts hyperscaler AI spend at $1T next year (+1% to GDP), and grid equipment is already recovering — GEV +6.15% and ETN +7.74% over the past month.
themes.label: Nuclear / AI power: demand story intact, prices washed out
themes.narrative: Uranium and nuclear-adjacent names are being sold as if the AI-power buildout stalled: CCJ and URA are 1-month laggards (-11.5% and -11.95%), SMR is down -14.21%.
themes.watchFor: VST revenue inflection flipping from DETERIORATING to RECOVERY, or continued insider buying in the IPPs.

themes.counterRead: MDB's decline reason is ACUTE_CATALYST rather than pure sentiment — the -23.1% monthly drop needs its trigger identified before it can be treated as sentiment noise. APP and NOW are the cleanest DATA_AHEAD setups (recovery confirmed, no catalyst flag); HUBS at -59.2% with RSI 40.6 needs the same catalyst audit as MDB. No conviction promotions were issued this cycle, so the pipeline is signaling watchlist-grade, not add-grade.
themes.dataAnchor: Revenue growth has not confirmed the obituary. NOW scored 71 on the watchlist promotion with revenue +23.1% YoY at -30.6% off its peak; APP holds a tier-B conviction score of 76 with 76% gross margins and a 60.8% FCF margin at -60.6% off its high (RSI 34.9); MDB scored 76 with revenue +22.8% YoY and 71.8% gross margins after a -23.1% single-month drop flagged as an acute catalyst. All four passed the 5-gate screening with a RESEARCH_SCREENED posture.
themes.label: Enterprise software: priced for obsolescence, still growing
themes.narrative: The market is pricing enterprise SaaS as AI roadkill: APP sits -60.6% off its 52-week high, HUBS -59.2%, TTD -78.4%, RDDT -45.9%, NOW -30.6%.
themes.watchFor: MDB's acute catalyst identified as sentiment vs fundamental; any tier-B name confirming the RECOVERY revenue inflection on next earnings.

themes.counterRead: The dispersion itself is the opportunity: the market pays full price for the capex spenders (META, NVDA) and discounts the suppliers, yet the suppliers' revenue growth is real. AVGO's tier-A score with earnings already past (Sep 2026) makes it the cleanest of the set — but as a holding, the zone logic and sizing already govern; the new information is that the setup is strengthening, not weakening. WDC's continued lag versus the equipment rebound flags memory as the weak sub-segment.
themes.dataAnchor: The suppliers feeding that capex trade at steep discounts: AVGO, a Core holding, is -29.1% off its high while growing revenue +23.9% YoY with 67.8% gross margins and a 42.1% FCF margin (top conviction score 81, tier A, 2-week window). The semi-equipment complex is rebounding from deep drawdowns — CLS +20.7%, AMAT +11.6%, KLAC +11.1%, LRCX +9.0% over the past month — while still 24-44% below their 52-week highs; WDC lags at -43.2% off its high. GOOGL (+2.86% 1m) adds the demand-side confirmation.
themes.label: AI hardware: hyperscalers priced for capex, suppliers left behind
themes.narrative: META ripped +26.97% over the past month and NVDA is only -3.4% off its 52-week high — the market believes hyperscaler AI capex is intact and accelerating.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding its tier-A score through its 2-week window; CLS sustaining its +20.7% monthly momentum above the 52-week-high discount.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree that higher-for-longer is a small-cap tax rather than a systemic threat — for now. The risk is a hot CPI print against the 2.35% breakeven repricing the front end and widening the IWM/SPY gap further. Soft-inflation headlines are already circulating (cooler-than-expected data shrugged off by the S&P), so the bar for a dovish surprise is higher than the bar for a hawkish one.
themes.dataAnchor: What higher-for-longer is breaking is small caps: IWM is -6.73% over three months while SPY is +3.27% over the same window. The curve is positively sloped (2s10s +0.37) and the 10Y breakeven is a contained 2.35%, so inflation expectations are not the driver — duration repricing is. Credit agrees: HY OAS 3.02 is nowhere near stress, and VIX at 16.29 is calm. The calendar holds the next repricing risk: CPI Sep prints Oct 14, FOMC Oct 27-28, then FOMC Dec 8-9.
themes.label: Rates: higher-for-longer bites the broad market, not credit
themes.narrative: A 5.29% 10-year with a 2.94% real yield and the Fed funds rate at 3.88% should be breaking something — yet equities sit near highs.
themes.watchFor: Oct 14 CPI Sep print versus the 2.35% 10Y breakeven; a widening of the IWM 3-month relative drag beyond -6.73%.

watchFor: HY OAS above 4.0 or SLOOS lifting off 0% — credit breaks the rotation read and forces a defensive posture.
Mag7-vs-SPY 52-week-high gap widening beyond ~12-15 points — rotation thesis strains under its own concentration.
Oct 14 CPI Sep print versus the 2.35% 10Y breakeven — a hot print reprices the front end and extends the IWM drag.
IWM 3-month relative performance: continued -6.73% drag means breadth never arrives; a close of the gap confirms broadening.
AVGO holding its tier-A 81 score through its 2-week window, and MDB's acute catalyst resolved as sentiment vs fundamental.
whereWaveBuilds: The next leg builds in the dislocated AI-power and software-supplier complex, where +18 to +28% YoY revenue growth sits under 26-61% drawdowns; the likely trigger is the Oct 14 CPI print and Oct 28 FOMC resetting rate expectations, which either releases the small-cap and breadth laggards or confirms the higher-for-longer drag.
